newsitem.title: CHINA: China finds new oil-bearing strata in western area.
newsitem.headline: China finds new oil-bearing strata in western area.

text.p: China has found 72 new oil-bearing strata in recent drilling in the Qaidam Basin in western Qinghai province as well as oil-rich structures in western Xinjiang, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

The drilling was done at the Xianliu well in the Qaidam Basin's Nanbaxian area, it said, quoting Ma Lining, chief geologist of the Prospecting and Development Institute of the Qinghai Petroleum Administration.
It was expected that reserves of 30 million tonnes of oil and gas would be verified at this well this year, Ma said.
Geological workers have also discovered an industrial oil gusher with a daily gas output exceeding 100,000 cubic metres at two other oil wells in the Nanbaxian region, he said.

Ma said there were high hopes for another medium-sized oil field at Nanbaxian, second only to the Ghasi Kola field, which has more than 100 million tonnes of oil and gas reserves and was discovered 20 years ago in the Qaidam Basin.
Nanbaxian region is one of eight key oil and gas prospecting and development areas designated by China National Oil Corporation as sites for breakthroughs this year, Xinhua said,
The Qaidam Basin now produces 4,300 tonnes of oil and gas daily, it said.
The Qinghai Petroleum Administration expects 40 billion cubic metres of newly-discovered geological gas reserves will be proven this year, it said.

The administration plans to increase the amount of verified oil and gas reserves to 600 million tonnes from the present 200 million tons and to raise annual gas output from the current 1.5 million tonnes to three million tonnes by 2000.
Geologists have also discovered a structure rich in oil and natural gas reserves in Kala Yorgun in the northern Tarim Basin in the Taklimakan desert in the neighbouring Xinjiang region, it said.
A test gas well sunk in the region by the Tarim Oil Exploration Headquarters last June showed good gas indications to a depth of 5,350 metres. Tests indicated high-yield industrial gas, it said.
It was the first high-yield gas well discovered in the Tarim Basin this year and a 60 square km area around the test well had conditions favorable for oil exploration, it said.
